03

Case study 1: Health Map

A team idea that earned 4★ for every member. The teacher’s message: “Govt is looking for any solution that addresses access issues. Add it to your NLP portfolio.”

The idea

A location-based, disease-aware healthcare recommendation system. It finds and ranks nearby healthcare facilities by the user’s location, each facility’s disease-specific treatment capability, and travel accessibility.

Research gaps

  • Disease-specific matching: finds centres that offer services for the particular disease.
  • Treatment availability: considers verified diagnostic and treatment capability.
  • Travel accessibility: ranks by road distance and estimated travel time.

How NLP is used

  • Extract services and treatment capabilities from facility descriptions and other text.
  • Identify disease names, services and search intent in natural-language queries.
  • Match different terms for the same disease or service with semantic similarity.
NERInformation ExtractionSemantic SimilarityText Classification

Team: Kondrarajender, Thaaruni, Harishankar, Lokesh, Varshini, Sathya Sree, Sharun

04

Case study 2: Word embeddings

Digital Assignment 1 (CSI4001, Natural Language Processing and Computational Linguistics), submitted on the VTOP portal. Question 3: how embeddings are built, what the baselines are, and which embeddings exist for Indian regional languages.

Download my submission (PDF)

What an embedding is

A word is turned into a vector, a list of real numbers. Words with similar meaning get nearby vectors, so “happy” and “joyful” sit close together while “happy” and “sad” sit far apart.

How embeddings are built

Corpus›Preprocess›Tokenize›Vocabulary / subwords›Train›Embedding matrix›Evaluate

Techniques covered

Word2Vec: CBOW predicts a word from its context, Skip-gram predicts the context from a word. GloVe: built from global word co-occurrence counts. BERT: contextual vectors that change with the sentence.

Word2VecGloVeBERT

Baselines

Bag of Words: counts only, sparse, no meaning. TF-IDF: counts weighted by how rare a word is. Embeddings beat both because they capture meaning.

BoWTF-IDF

Indian-language embeddings

IndicNLP library (Tamil, Hindi, Bengali, Telugu, Malayalam), IndicBERT by AI4Bharat (11 languages), iNLTK (Gujarati, Marathi, Kannada) and FastText (157 languages).

IndicBERTFastText

Demonstrations

  • Similarity: Tamil மரம் (tree) is near செடி (plant) and காடு (forest).
  • Analogy: Hindi राजा − पुरुष + महिला ≈ रानी.
  • Sentiment: a Telugu movie review classified as positive.
  • NER: “Ravi visited Chennai yesterday” gives PERSON, LOCATION, DATE.

import nltk
from nltk.corpus import inaugural
from nltk.corpus import stopwords

# Load Harrison's inaugural speech
text = inaugural.words('1841-Harrison.txt')

# Convert to lowercase and keep only alphabetic words
words = [w.lower() for w in text if w.isalpha()]

# Remove stopwords
stop_words = set(stopwords.words('english'))
filtered_words = [w for w in words if w not in stop_words]

# Frequency Distribution
fd = nltk.FreqDist(filtered_words)

print("Top 20 Frequent Words")
print(fd.most_common(20))

# Long words (length >= 12)
print("\nLong Words")
long_words = sorted(set([w for w in filtered_words if len(w) >= 12]))

for word in long_words:
    print(word, "Length =", len(word))

Project writeup

Tap a heading to open it.

1Title
Sensorless NEAT Estimation via Multilingual NLP and Physics-Informed Hybrid Modeling
Sharun Kumar D (23MID0131) and Kishore Kannan G (23MID0414), VIT Vellore.
2Motivation
Non-Exercise Activity Thermogenesis (NEAT) is the energy we burn through everyday movement such as walking, standing and chores. It matters for weight and metabolic health, but most people cannot measure it. We wanted a person to be able to simply say or type what they did, in the language they speak, and get a trustworthy number with a reason behind it.
3Existing gap that motivated the project
  • Hardware dependency: accurate NEAT tracking needs wearables that many people do not own or wear all day.
  • Language barrier: apps expect English dropdowns, but users naturally say “Naan 30 minutes nadanthen” or mix languages.
  • Context-blind formulas: a fixed MET × weight formula ignores heat, humidity and accumulated fatigue.
  • Black-box answers: users get a calorie number with no explanation.
4Architecture
Mobile app›FastAPI›Whisper + Gemini NLP›MET mapping›NMFN model›SHAP + fatigue›SQLite history

Five layers: user input, language and NLP, data and context, hybrid estimation (the Neuro-Metabolic Fusion Network, NMFN), and output and explainability. The numerical branch (weight, MET, temperature, humidity) and an RNN sequence branch are joined by a fusion gate. A physiological cap of 25 kcal/kg/h, scaled by duration, bounds the result, and the training loss penalises any prediction above the human limit.

5Complete tech stack
LayerTechnology
Mobile appReact Native, Expo, TypeScript, react-native-chart-kit, expo-av (voice), expo-location
BackendPython, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic, httpx
Speech and NLPWhisper (Hugging Face Transformers), Gemini (schema-constrained JSON), XLM-RoBERTa token classification, librosa, torchaudio
ModellingPyTorch (RNN/LSTM branch, fusion gate), XGBoost, scikit-learn
ExplainabilitySHAP (GradientExplainer), fatigue forecast
Data and contextSQLite, OpenWeatherMap API
6Datasets used
  • 2024 Adult Compendium of Physical Activities: reference MET values for each activity.
  • PAMAP2 Physical Activity Monitoring dataset: activity sequences used for the sequence branch.
  • OpenWeatherMap (live): temperature and humidity for the user’s location.
  • User data: profile (weight, intensity) and saved workout history in SQLite.
7Prompts used

In-app prompt (Gemini semantic extraction, from the backend):

You are an expert Biomechanical Data Scientist and a native speaker of English, Tamil, and colloquial Tanglish. Your job is to extract highly accurate Metabolic Equivalent of Task (MET) scores and durations from unstructured, messy user inputs.

1. Deep Semantic Extraction: read the input naturally; understand all tenses, slang, typos and mixed languages.
2. Dynamic MET Retrieval: no hardcoded lists; use knowledge of the Compendium of Physical Activities to assign the exact MET.
3. Contextual Stacking: for overlapping activities (e.g. walking while talking), compute a combined MET.
If duration is not mentioned, default to the given number of minutes.

Output ONLY raw JSON: {"duration_mins": int, "base_met": float, "detected_activity": "clear english summary"}
Transcript: "{transcript}"

Prompts used to build the app: paste the prompts you gave your AI coding agent here (project master prompt, backend prompt, UI prompt), each in its own box.

8NLP pipeline
1 Capture text/voice›2 Speech to text (Whisper)›3 Language detection›4 Entity extraction (Action, Duration, Environment)›5 LLM semantic parsing to JSON›6 Normalise to Compendium MET›7 Contextual stacking

The output of the pipeline (activity, duration, MET) is handed to the NMFN along with weight, weather and history. Course concepts used: tokenization, normalization, NER, code-mixed text handling and semantic extraction.

9Users, inputs and outputs
UsersAnyone who wants to track everyday activity without a wearable: students, office workers, people who think in Tamil, Hindi or Tanglish.
InputsText: “I walked for 30 minutes”, “Naan 30 minutes nadanthen”.
Voice: recorded audio (uploaded to /process-audio).
Profile: weight and intensity. Context: GPS location for weather.
OutputsDetected activity, duration, MET, calories in kcal, SHAP feature-importance chart, 4-hour fatigue forecast, and saved workout history on a dashboard.
Example“I walked for 2hrs”, 100 kg, Normal intensity gives walking, 120 min, MET 3.5, 510.8 kcal.
10References
  • Herrmann, S. D. et al. 2024 Adult Compendium of Physical Activities.
  • Reiss, A. and Stricker, D. PAMAP2 Physical Activity Monitoring dataset, UCI Machine Learning Repository.
  • Radford, A. et al. Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision (Whisper), 2022.
  • Conneau, A. et al. Unsupervised Cross-lingual Representation Learning at Scale (XLM-RoBERTa), 2020.
  • Lundberg, S. and Lee, S.-I. A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions (SHAP), 2017.
  • FastAPI, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, React Native and Expo documentation.
